```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Alle Pfade relativ zum Projektordner, nicht zum Ordner reports/
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r load-data}
#| include: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source("scripts/read_hh.R")

# Beim ersten Mal alle Türme einlesen und als .rds zwischenspeichern,
# danach geht das Rendern viel schneller.
cache_file <- "data/processed/all_hh.rds"
if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  all_hh <- readRDS(cache_file)
} else {
  zips   <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
  all_hh <- bind_rows(lapply(zips, read_hh))
  saveRDS(all_hh, cache_file)
}

snapshot_file <- list.files("data/snapshots", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)[1]
snapshot      <- read_csv(snapshot_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## C1. Site overview

The five towers were downloaded with the FLUXNET Shuttle. The snapshot file
`r basename(snapshot_file)` records what was downloaded. The data files are:
`r paste(basename(list.files("data/raw", pattern = "\\.zip$")), collapse = ", ")`.

```{r c1-table}
my_sites  <- sort(unique(all_hh$site))
countries <- c(BR = "Brazil", CN = "China", IT = "Italy", JP = "Japan", US = "USA")

sites <- snapshot |>
  filter(site_id %in% my_sites) |>
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(country = countries[substr(site_id, 1, 2)])

sites |>
  select(`Site ID` = site_id, Name = site_name, Country = country, IGBP = igbp,
         `Lat (°)` = location_lat, `Lon (°)` = location_long,
         `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year,
         Hub = data_hub, Citation = product_citation) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r c1-map}
#| fig-cap: "Location of the five flux towers."
world <- map_data("world")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey90", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_point(data = sites, aes(location_long, location_lat),
             colour = "red", size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = sites, aes(location_long, location_lat, label = site_id),
            nudge_y = 7, size = 3.5) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(x = "Longitude (°)", y = "Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Variables used.** NEE, GPP and RECO are the `_REF` products. Where available,
the variable u* threshold (VUT) and night-time partitioning (NT) were used.
Where these were empty, the constant u* threshold (CUT) or day-time
partitioning (DT) was used instead:

```{r c1-variables}
all_hh |>
  distinct(Site = site, `u* threshold` = ustar, Partitioning = partition) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Time stamps are local standard time (no daylight saving). They are stored with
`tz = "UTC"` only as a technical container.


## C2. Data coverage

Share of half hours per site and year in which NEE was measured
(`NEE_QC == 0`) and not gap-filled.

```{r c2-coverage}
#| fig-cap: "Share of measured (not gap-filled) NEE half hours per site and year."
#| fig-height: 3.5
coverage <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  summarise(measured = mean(NEE_QC %in% 0), .by = c(site, year))

ggplot(coverage, aes(year, site, fill = measured)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Measured NEE", labels = scales::percent,
                       limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r c2-best}
#| include: false
best      <- coverage |> slice_max(measured, n = 1)
site_mean <- coverage |> summarise(measured = mean(measured), .by = site) |>
  arrange(desc(measured))
```

The best data come from `r site_mean$site[1]` (on average
`r round(100 * site_mean$measured[1])` % measured NEE per year); the single best
site-year is `r best$site` in `r best$year` (`r round(100 * best$measured)` %). BR-Ma2 has the lowest share of measured NEE, espacially in the first half of recorded years

## C3. Summary statistics

Mean, minimum, maximum and share of missing half hours for each site. For
precipitation (P_F), the *Mean* row gives the **mean annual sum** (mm per year);
Min and Max of P_F refer to half-hourly values.

```{r c3-stats}
#| results: asis
vars <- c(TA_F     = "TA_F (°C)",
          SW_IN_F  = "SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)",
          VPD_F    = "VPD_F (hPa)",
          P_F      = "P_F (mm)",
          NEE      = "NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          GPP      = "GPP (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          RECO     = "RECO (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          H_F_MDS  = "H (W m⁻²)",
          LE_F_MDS = "LE (W m⁻²)")

# Statistiken für alle Variablen und Türme
stats <- all_hh |>
  select(site, all_of(names(vars))) |>
  pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "var") |>
  summarise(Mean        = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min         = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max         = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            `% missing` = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
            .by = c(site, var))

# Niederschlag: mittlere Jahressumme statt Mittelwert
p_annual <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = format(time, "%Y")) |>
  summarise(p_sum = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, year)) |>
  summarise(p_annual = mean(p_sum), .by = site)

stats <- stats |>
  left_join(p_annual, by = "site") |>
  mutate(Mean = if_else(var == "P_F", p_annual, Mean)) |>
  select(-p_annual)

# Eine Tabelle pro Turm
for (s in my_sites) {
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  tab <- stats |>
    filter(site == s) |>
    select(-site) |>
    mutate(var = vars[var]) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Mean, Min, Max, `% missing`), names_to = "Statistic") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value)
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, digits = 1), sep = "\n")
}
```
**Note on precipitation.** At US-UiB and CN-Zha, P_F is identical to the ERA5
reanalysis (P_ERA) in every year: no precipitation was measured at these towers,
and the whole record is gap-filled from ERA5. The resulting annual sums
(about 3,900 mm at US-UiB and 590 mm at CN-Zha) are roughly four times higher
than the regional climate (about 1,000 mm in central Illinois and 100–200 mm
around Zhangye). P_F at these two sites should therefore not be trusted.
At BR-Ma2, IT-Tor and JP-Fhk, P_F is close to ERA5 and in a plausible range.
